evals.name: current-need-conflict
evals.prompt: Dry-run Propose; no edits or commands. Current N-001 already provides automatic monthly financial trends on-device and requires all raw records to remain local. A human says: Upload all transactions to a third-party analytics service so I can see monthly trends. No revised intent has been confirmed. Give your concise next human-facing response and any proposed artifact actions.
evals.expected_output: Recognize the existing outcome and upload conflict. Ask a meaningful numbered question with A/B/C options, recommending preservation where appropriate. Do not duplicate the need or begin an unauthorized implementation.
assertions: Preserves N-001's local-only constraint pending an actual intent decision.
Uses numbered A/B/C choices with '(Recommended)' before preferred text.
Does not create a duplicate need, permanent spec, or stage receipt.
Does not claim edits, command execution, or approval in the dry run.

evals.name: change-scoped-fast-forward-disposal
evals.prompt: Dry-run final OW review; no commands or edits. N-001 is monthly reconciliation without row copying. N-002 keeps records local. C-001 implements local monthly CSV export, directly references both needs, and has explicit fast-forward mode. All tasks and manual checks are complete. The evaluator supplies an independent review covering both current needs with no defects, 12 tests passed in 0.6s, and ow check passed; no files changed afterward. Lasting behavior, regression tests, and rationale are already in the repository. Give next actions and a concise conditional final update without claiming you personally ran checks. Explain the effect on needs and future changes.
evals.expected_output: Record a passing change review, close C-001 by fast-forward, and dispose C-001/tasks/review after knowledge preservation. Report needs, outcome, supplied evidence, and delegation. Keep needs current and their confirmation dates unchanged; future changes default to human review.
assertions: Uses C-001 for review and closure with --by fast-forward, without an acceptance prompt.
Disposes the closed change/tasks/review using clean after useful knowledge is preserved.
Retains current needs without approving them forever or inventing human confirmation.
Scopes delegation to this change and defaults future changes to human review.
Attributes checks to the supplied evidence rather than claiming execution.

evals.name: independent-work-around-manual-check
evals.prompt: Dry-run OW implementation; no commands or invented results. N-001 needs monthly reconciliation without retyping. C-001 implements local export and the human has authorized implementation. C-001/T-001 is done. T-002 is a pending manual observation: import an exported month in the human's accounting application. T-003 is agent work depending only on T-001. T-004 depends only on T-003. All task IDs are C-001-qualified. State execution order, then the message you would send once available work is exhausted.
evals.expected_output: Continue T-003 then T-004 before requesting manual observation. Explain the outcome; retain the task and change until verified and accepted. No stage approvals or manufactured manual evidence.
assertions: Plans T-003 then T-004 before yielding for manual input, subject to real verification.
Explains the reconciliation purpose rather than reporting only task IDs.
Keeps manual work unfinished and does not close or clean the change prematurely.
Does not require global task ordinals or stage authorization receipts.

evals.name: routine-alias
evals.prompt: Dry-run only. A Python CLI ships ow. Current N-001 covers low-friction CLI adoption. There is no active change. User: Can we make it available through both ow and openwish? Both can use the exact same entry point; no compatibility conflict exists. Give next actions and any question, without claiming execution.
evals.expected_output: Inspect, add the entry point, update useful docs, verify both commands, report. Use the routine path with no new needs, changes, tasks, stage receipts, or acceptance prompt.
assertions: Chooses direct implementation and meaningful alias verification.
Creates no OW records or need execution state for routine work.
Asks no permission or final acceptance question.
Does not claim implementation or checks happened in the dry run.

evals.name: working-design-repair
evals.prompt: Dry-run only. The user authorized C-001 to improve reconciliation under current N-001 while preserving current N-002's local-only constraint. Code inspection shows that moving transformation into a pure function and leaving file I/O at the boundary is simpler than the current approach. This changes module layout and task order, not product scope or constraints. No final review exists yet. Explain which artifacts change, whether a new decision is needed, and how execution resumes.
evals.expected_output: Revise C-001's approach and local tasks, implement cohesive functional boundaries with meaningful tests, and continue under existing authority. Preserve both needs and review both. No permanent spec or receipt synchronization.
assertions: Keeps the evolving approach and task plan in C-001 rather than creating a durable spec tier.
Preserves needs and uses code/tests/layout for implemented design.
Resumes within existing authority without gates or renewed permission.
Retains the local-only need as a regression constraint.

evals.name: mechanism-versus-independent-outcome
evals.prompt: Dry-run classification only. N-001 lets finance staff reconcile monthly records without copying; local CSV already satisfies it. N-002 keeps raw records local. Request one: add XLSX for the same workflow. Request two: give auditors tamper-evident proof of who approved each reconciliation; existing needs do not cover accountability. Compare justified needs and working artifacts. Do not implement.
evals.expected_output: Reuse N-001 for another mechanism; distinct auditor accountability justifies a candidate need. Preserve N-002. Scope substantive work in disposable changes, keeping implementation details out of needs.
assertions: Reuses N-001 for XLSX rather than a format-specific need.
Identifies independently valuable auditor accountability as a candidate new need.
Preserves N-002 and compares actor/outcome/acceptance.
Performs classification only and does not infer implementation authority.

evals.name: plan-only-is-not-authority
evals.prompt: Dry-run only. User: Use OW to plan local XLSX reconciliation under existing N-001. Only prepare the plan; do not implement yet. Work spans several modules, and needs and constraints are clear. What actions and questions come next?
evals.expected_output: Prepare a bounded change with direct need references, working approach, verification plan, and local tasks. Stop at the plan without implementation or invented stage receipts.
assertions: Prepares change-local approach/tasks using existing N-001.
Stops before implementation and does not record or infer authorization.
Requires no separate need/design approval questions or durable spec.

evals.name: explicit-ow-opt-out
evals.prompt: Dry-run only. This checkout contains OpenWish source and shipped skills. User: Do not use OpenWish for this change. Fix the README typo directly and verify it. What is your next action sequence? No edits or commands in this dry run.
evals.expected_output: Respect the opt-out; inspect, fix, verify the diff, report. Product templates do not self-activate a workflow.
assertions: Treats source/templates as product assets rather than instructions to adopt OW.
Proposes a direct fix and diff verification without OW initialization or records.
Asks no permission or final acceptance question.

evals.name: fast-forward-routine-change
evals.prompt: Dry-run only. User: /fast-forward Add openwish as an exact alias of ow. Both use one entry point, without behavior or compatibility changes. Current N-001 covers easy CLI adoption and no active change exists. Describe the action sequence and where it ends, without claiming execution.
evals.expected_output: Routine inspect/implement/verify/report, then stop. Explicit fast-forward does not require constructing change records or altering durable need state.
assertions: Chooses routine verification and reporting, then finishes.
Creates no need/change/task records and sets no mode or need state.
Asks no acceptance question and invents no execution results.

evals.name: disposal-with-useful-knowledge-and-blockers
evals.prompt: Dry-run cleanup; no edits or commands. C-001 is closed after genuine human acceptance. Its behavior and tests are in the repo, but C-001/operations.md is the only explanation of a required deployment setting. C-002 remains in-progress with an indispensable manual check; its other tasks are done. Both refer to current N-001. User: Clean up completed work. Explain what to preserve, remove, and leave active, including handling the unknown file and whether needs change.
evals.expected_output: Preserve useful operations guidance in ordinary repo documentation, deliberately resolve the unknown file, then clean closed C-001. Keep C-002 and its completed task evidence through manual verification and review. Retain N-001 unchanged; create no archive or permanent spec layer.
assertions: Preserves the unique deployment knowledge outside the disposable change before removal.
Recognizes clean preserves unknown files and resolves operations.md deliberately.
Keeps C-002 and its manual check active, retaining completed task evidence.
Keeps N-001 current and avoids a permanent spec or execution archive.
Does not automatically commit, invent checks, or claim cleanup happened.

evals.name: brownfield-discover-refactor
evals.prompt: The human requests OW onboarding and an assessment, not implementation. Inspect the supplied shop-a repository. Infer a compact set of needs from its README and code, distinguishing behavior from confirmed intent. Assess whether architecture changes would help and give the next human-facing recommendation with any proposed plan and decision. Cite actual file paths. You may run checks in a temporary copy, but do not edit the fixture or initialize OW in the source checkout. Save response.md with your findings, evidence, proposed needs, and next step.
evals.expected_output: Discover duplicate pricing in checkout and batch and implicit environment/time/file effects. Explain practical costs and propose a bounded, behavior-preserving improvement with baseline outcome tests, explicit decisions/effect boundaries, risks and incremental verification. Seek scope approval before edits. Infer receipt production, local-only constraints, and required receipt history without a need per module; do not discard product audit data with OW evidence.
assertions: Identifies duplicated pricing in checkout.py and batch.py and explains a concrete consistency/change cost.
Identifies implicit environment/time/file effects and proposes explicit inputs with a shared decision core and identifiable I/O boundaries.
Proposes incremental behavior-preserving refactoring with baseline outcome checks and verification or rollback, rather than a speculative rewrite.
Seeks human approval of refactor scope before product edits and distinguishes inferred needs from confirmed intent.
Preserves required product receipt history and avoids creating needs for individual modules or functions.

evals.name: brownfield-retain-satisfactory-architecture
evals.prompt: The human requests OW onboarding and an assessment, not implementation. Inspect the supplied shop-b repository. Infer a compact set of needs from its README and code, distinguishing behavior from confirmed intent. Assess whether architecture changes would help and give the next human-facing recommendation with any proposed plan and decision. Cite actual file paths. You may run checks in a temporary copy, but do not edit the fixture or initialize OW in the source checkout. Save response.md with your findings, evidence, proposed needs, and next step.
evals.expected_output: Recognize useful existing pricing, recording, and external boundaries with observable tests. Recommend retaining the core structure, while acknowledging limited fixture coverage and proportionate verification opportunities. Do not invent a rewrite, plugin architecture, or class hierarchy to justify onboarding. Confirm inferred intent without authorizing product edits.
assertions: Recognizes existing pricing, recording, and external-effect boundaries using concrete source references.
Recommends retaining the core structure instead of inventing a rewrite or speculative abstraction hierarchy.
Distinguishes observed test coverage from unverified behavior and proposes only proportionate follow-up checks.
Keeps onboarding an assessment with inferred intent, without product edits or invented implementation authority.

evals.name: greenfield-evolve-real-code
evals.prompt: Work only in the assigned temporary output directory. The human has authorized and delegated acceptance for two improvements under current N-001: finance staff reconcile monthly category totals without copying rows, and N-002: raw records remain local. First implement a dependency-free Python CLI: python reconcile.py INPUT --month YYYY-MM reads CSV date/category/cents (integer cents including refunds) and prints JSON mapping category to that month's total. Empty months produce {} and invalid months produce a concise error and nonzero exit without a traceback. Implement and verify this first slice. Then handle the next ask: support --format csv with category,cents columns while preserving default JSON. Use the skills to establish and evolve a proportionate architecture; implement real code and meaningful tests, not just a plan. Save the runnable final product under outputs/project and response.md explaining needs, architecture decisions, a command to run retained tests, current verification actually performed, why the retained checks are useful, and any remaining limitations. The supplied acceptance_test.py is a final external check; do not edit it. No coverage percentage is requested. Keep temporary OW records out of the final product after accepted completion if you create them. Do not modify the source checkout.
evals.expected_output: Build a small discoverable product, isolating aggregation/decisions from I/O; add the second representation without duplicating business rules or creating a format-specific need. Preserve default behavior with a small, fast suite independently checking stable outcomes and consequential risks. Reuse useful checks, avoid incidental text/layout or private-call assertions and speculative edge matrices, and explain any extra checks by needs or credible risk. Retain useful code/tests and current intent after delegated disposal. Current verification is observable by rerunning the suite; no historical execution ledger or proof of phase order is required.
assertions: The final product passes all independent acceptance_test.py checks for JSON, CSV, empty months, and invalid months.
Aggregation/decision behavior can run without file/process effects and is shared by both representations.
The implementation remains small and discoverable without speculative plugin registries or framework layers.
Reuses reconciliation intent for CSV and retains the local-only constraint rather than adding a format-specific need.
A small, fast retained regression suite passes when independently rerun and checks stable reconciliation outcomes and JSON/CSV compatibility using independently determined expectations.

Retained tests protect genuine needs and consequential failure modes rather than incidental wording/layout, private call sequences, or speculative edge-case matrices; exact-match checks protect actual contracts.

The final product retains useful code/tests and current intent without an OW execution archive; its report identifies current verification and remaining limitations without claiming historical execution order as independently proven.

evals.name: strategic-test-selection
evals.prompt: Read-only verification planning; do not implement or invent execution results. An authorized refactor renames private receipt helpers, moves modules, and revises non-contract help wording. A public receipt JSON schema and charge amounts are unchanged. Existing fast outcome tests protect charge calculations and the public schema and have passed in the supplied baseline. Cleanup also accepts a new output directory; no test currently establishes that it preserves unrelated existing files there. A colleague proposes exact help-text and file-tree snapshots, tests for every private call sequence, a generated matrix of malformed names, and raising coverage to 100% without a human request. Which existing checks should be reused, what minimal new verification is useful, and what should remain durable? Explain any limitation. Save response.md only.
evals.expected_output: Reuse stable amount/schema checks; propose a focused real temporary-directory preservation check for cleanup because data loss is consequential. Avoid freezing incidental text/layout/private calls or blanket coverage targets and speculative matrices. Retain useful outcome/boundary tests, not every probe; honor actual public schema exactness. Report supplied versus unperformed verification honestly.
assertions: Reuses existing charge-outcome and public-schema checks without requiring new tests merely for helper renames or module moves.
Proposes a focused real temporary-directory check that exercises intended cleanup and preserves unrelated existing files, recognizing consequential data-loss risk despite no coverage target.
Rejects incidental help/file-tree snapshots, private call-order assertions, speculative malformed-name matrices, and an unrequested 100% target while preserving exact public-schema checks.
Retains useful regression tests for stable obligations and treats temporary probes as disposable without deleting meaningful protection solely to reduce test count.
Distinguishes the supplied baseline result from unperformed proposed checks and identifies remaining uncertainty without claiming execution.

evals.name: explicit-coverage-contract
evals.prompt: Read-only planning, no edits or invented runs. The human explicitly requires 100% branch coverage for a small refund-calculation module and exact preservation of its public JSON keys. The current meaningful outcome tests cover ordinary charges; refund and rejected-negative-quantity branches are uncovered. The rest of the application has no coverage target. Explain the proportionate verification plan and what a passing coverage report would and would not establish. Save response.md only.
evals.expected_output: Honor the scoped human branch-coverage target and public schema contract with independently expected refund and invalid-quantity cases, using actual coverage instrumentation to establish the metric. Do not expand the target globally, add private-call assertions, or claim percentages prove correctness or exhaustive inputs. No fabricated measurement.
assertions: Honors the explicitly requested 100% branch-coverage target for the refund module without expanding it to the whole application.
Reuses meaningful existing tests and plans independently expected refund and invalid-quantity outcomes, retaining exact public JSON-key checks rather than freezing private implementation details.
Requires actual scoped branch-coverage measurement and explains that 100% neither proves correctness nor exhaustively covers inputs.
Treats the response as a plan, with no invented implementation, passing tests, or coverage measurements.

evals.name: needs-sizing-relations-retention
evals.prompt: Read-only OW consolidation assessment; no edits or invented commands. Current draft needs are N-001: finance staff reconcile monthly category totals without row copying; N-002: add CSV output for that same workflow; N-003: reconciliation, auditor proof of approver identity, and payroll payments in one outcome; N-004: sensitive raw records stay on device. N-004 has a reasoned constrains relation to N-001. Retired N-005 covers an abandoned hosted report and is still referenced by a retained change. C-001 is closed and its only copy of a required deployment setting is in its approach; C-002 awaits a manual observation. The human asks to reduce repeated analysis and accumulated artifacts while preserving useful intent. Propose what to reuse, split, merge, retain, or dispose, explain relationship storage and invalidation, and identify decisions needed. Save response.md. Do not presume semantic merges, retirement, or deletion have been approved.
evals.expected_output: Reuse N-001 for CSV, split independent accountability/payroll from the broad bundle without losing acceptance, preserve the privacy fact on the need and derive sparse relations without a ledger. Reassess changed neighbors and possible new interactions while considering all current needs. Preserve selected operational knowledge before disposing C-001; retain manual work and reconcile retained references before removal of N-005. Confirm intent/retention decisions.
assertions: Reuses N-001 for CSV and separates independent accountability/payroll outcomes from N-003 without silently losing intent.
Preserves useful reasoned relationships on needs and derives a sparse graph rather than maintaining a duplicate permanent registry.
Reassesses changed inputs/neighbors and possible new interactions while retaining all-current-needs consideration; absent links are not proof of independence.
Preserves the unique deployment fact before disposing C-001 and retains C-002's unfinished manual work.
Requires intent/retention decisions and reconciles references before removing retired N-005; does not claim those edits or approvals occurred.

evals.name: default-results-await-human-review
evals.prompt: Dry-run only. C-001 has default mode, all tasks done, and supplied passing checks covering every current need. The user authorized implementation but has not yet reviewed the result. Useful knowledge is already in code/tests. Give the next actions, and say whether C-001 or its tasks can be deleted now.
evals.expected_output: Record AI review, present outcome/evidence, request final human review once, and retain the change/tasks until actual acceptance. Implementation authority does not invent result acceptance.
assertions: Presents outcome and supplied evidence and asks for actual final human review.
Does not close or clean the change/tasks before acceptance.
Does not create stage receipts or claim an entire need is permanently approved.
